gloss: scholarly temperament; academic bent; scholar type

definitions.explanation: Describes a person whose natural disposition is toward academic study and research. Such a person is typically focused, detail-oriented, and more interested in learning than in practical or commercial pursuits.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{学究|がっきゅう}{肌|はだ}の{人|ひと}で、{休|やす}みの{日|ひ}も{研究室|けんきゅうしつ}にいる。
examples.english: He has a scholarly temperament and is in the lab even on days off.

examples.japanese: {学究|がっきゅう}{肌|はだ}の{先生|せんせい}だから、{説明|せつめい}が{細|こま}かくて{助|たす}かる。
examples.english: Because the teacher has an academic bent, the detailed explanations are helpful.

examples.japanese: {学究|がっきゅう}{肌|はだ}なところはあるが、{実務|じつむ}もしっかりこなす{人物|じんぶつ}だ。
examples.english: While having a scholarly disposition, he is a person who also handles practical affairs thoroughly.

notes:
{学究|がっきゅう} means scholarly pursuit or academic study; {肌|はだ} literally means skin but as a suffix means temperament or natural disposition.

THE 〜{肌|はだ} SUFFIX:
Attaches to nouns to mean "having the temperament/character of ~":
- {学究|がっきゅう}{肌|はだ}: scholarly type
- {芸術家|げいじゅつか}{肌|はだ}: artistic type
- {商人|しょうにん}{肌|はだ}: merchant type; business-minded
- {職人|しょくにん}{肌|はだ}: artisan type; hands-on craftsman type
